Pakruojis Jewish Cemetery 1

Jewish Cemetery · Šiaulių apskritis, Lithuania

Demolished. This is the first and oldest of Pakruojis's Jewish cemeteries, on the town-side bank of the Kruoja River, used until the early 1800s; per the testimony of the community's rabbi in 1932, one of its ancient headstones bore an inscription dating to 1761, though this can no longer be verified since the cemetery no longer exists. During the Nazi occupation, the Germans destroyed the site, taking its gravestones to the local mill to be pulverized; after the war, Soviet soldiers who died fighting the Germans in 1944 were buried there instead, and a Soviet memorial now stands at the site's entrance. Pakruojis's own 1801 summer synagogue, reconstructed in 2017, is today the oldest wooden synagogue in Lithuania, now housing the children's section of the local public library.
